result.title: Agent-as-a-Verifier: From Scores to Evidence for General Verification
result.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development
result.summary: Verification is increasingly critical across various inference and learning paradigms, such as test-time scaling, recursive intelligence and automated research, where feedback can improve efficiency and optimization. Common score-based verifiers, or discriminative reward models, predict a scalar reward for an output. While useful for filtering, rewarding, and ranking, such scores provide no explicit, auditable evidentiary basis for the judgment. In parallel, although existing generative process reward models offer text feedback, most designs do not fully exploit agentic capabilities, such as tool use and iterative reasoning, which are essential for fact-checking and fine-grained claim verification. In this paper, we address these limitations by introducing Agent-as-a-Verifier, an agentic, certificate-producing verification system that places role-separated LLM agents inside a formal-methods-inspired claim-obligation-certificate protocol. Given a generation candidate, Agent-as-a-Verifier produces a certificate by extracting a verdict-blind dependency graph of claims, independently compiling the task's acceptance contract, and deriving checkable obligations. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, Agent-as-a-Verifier achieves higher accuracy than the state-of-the-art approach. Across different downstream applications, the augmented agent also outperforms the plain agent on FrontierMath and CyberGym. More importantly, Agent-as-a-Verifier is able to identify reward-hacking solutions that deceive the benchmark evaluator, highlighting its broader potential for iterative and recursive agent optimization. Code is available at https://github.com/sunyxedu/General-Verifier

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Agent-as-a-Verifier，把角色分离的 LLM agent 放入形式化方法风格的「主张—义务—证书」协议：先从候选输出抽取与结论无关的依赖图、独立编译验收契约并生成可核查义务，从而产出可审计的证据证书而非标量分数；在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上准确率超过已有方法，并能识别欺骗评测器的 reward hacking 解。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用可核查证据与义务分解替代标量奖励的验证协议，可能为核查 LVR 推理轨迹中视觉证据是否被真正使用、以及 latent 步骤的贡献分配提供线索，但原文面向文本 agent 任务，未涉及视觉或多模态，需较多核查。
